facts.text: The historic Oliver Estate, built in the 1700s by Judge Peter Oliver, hosts a colonial reenactment that lets visitors step back into 18th‑century life.
During the reenactment, actors demonstrate colonial military drills, musket firing, and hands‑on spinning, weaving, and cooking, while children play colonial‑themed games.
Middleborough was first settled by Europeans in 1661, originally called Nemasket before adopting the name Middleborough in 1669.
Every December, the Oliver Estate turns into a winter wonderland for Christmas celebrations, with a tree‑lighting ceremony at 5:00 PM on the 13th, 14th, 20th, and 21st.
The Oliver Estate’s deep ties to the American Revolution make it a perfect backdrop for living‑history events that highlight the town’s patriotic past.
Middleborough Center sits at 41°53′39″N 70°55′9″W, a precise geographic marker that places it firmly in southeastern Massachusetts.
